items.title: General Public Comment
Report of the General Manager
FY 2023-24 Capital Financing Plan Update
items.text: FY 2023-24 Capital Financing Plan Update Nikolai Skarloff, Capital Finance Director began with an overview of debt management and stated that there is a large outstanding debt portfolio and significant projected future debt issuance and credit needs. He noted that activities are guided by Commission policies, the Revenue Bond Oversight Committee, and the annual Capital Financing Plan. Director Skarloff stated the SFPUC has $8.5 billion of outstanding borrowing that excludes $3.6 billion of undrawn Commercial Paper, Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act, and State Revolving Fund borrowing. He indicated the 10-Year Financial Plan includes $6.338 billion of additional borrowing. He provided a summary of Enterprise debt and Enterprise Capital Ratings. Director Skarloff reviewed new money/credit needs, administration of existing debt portfolio, and market opportunities. He provided current market conditions and stated (1) Federal Reserve has significantly raised rates and is forecasted to purse rate hikes for the remainder of 2023, with a decrease anticipated in 2024; (2) Yield inversion persists in the municipal market; and (3) Volatility in both the taxable and tax-exempt markets remain and create potential for new refunding opportunities. Director Skarloff briefly reviewed the FY2023-24 Capital Financing Plan and described other initiatives including the Alternative Water Supply, managing risk in a rising rate environment. items.title: Accept work performed by Precision Engineering, Inc
items.text: Accept work performed by Precision Engineering, Inc. under Contract No. WW-677, Various Locations Sewer Replacement No. 6, for a total contract amount of $4,401,284 and a total contract duration of 564 consecutive calendar days; and authorize final payment to the contractor. Commissioner Stacy addressed item 7a and expressed thanks that the data gathered from the air quality monitors will be made available to the public. In response to a question from Commissioner Stacy regarding item 7e as to why there is no increase in funding being requested, Barbara Palacios, Project Manager stated that staff are waiting for a quote for replacement of the equipment and have not started negotiations with the contractor for a contract extension, and at the appropriate time staff will return to the Commission to request funding for a contract extension. Project Manager Palacios and Assistant General Manager Robinson responded to a follow- up question regarding corrosion and equipment maintenance. Commissioner Maxwell requested periodic updates as appropriate. Brief discussion ensued

items.title: Approve the Ocean Beach Climate Change Adaptation Project, Long-Term Improvements, a multi-city-department project led by the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission
items.text: Approve the Ocean Beach Climate Change Adaptation Project, Long-Term Improvements, a multi-city-department project led by the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission; authorize staff to proceed with actions necessary to implement the Project; approve a letter of agreement describing the terms of an anticipated Memorandum of Understanding with the San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department regarding construction and operation of the Project improvements and authorize the General Manager to negotiate and execute the same; urge the San Francisco Recreation and Parks Commission and the Board of Supervisors to restrict vehicular traffic on the Great Highway Extension and take any other actions necessary to facilitate the Project; and adopt findings and a Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act. Anna Roche, Project Manager reviewed the historic approach to coastal erosion and temporary protection measures and reviewed the Ocean Beach major project components. She continued with discussion of the protection of the Lake Merced Tunnel at Ocean Beach. She provided images of Ocean Beach now and with anticipated work completed. Project Manager Roche discussed the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency’s Westside Traffic Flow Strategy. She concluded with a summary of the requested Commission approval action and noted future approvals that will be brought to the Commission for the project. Project Manager Roche responded
